note: Reserved-name check uses the raw name instead of the normalised key, so 'Admin' slips through. Fix in check_username: test `key`.
Username-in-password check is case-sensitive; docstring says any case. Fix in check_password: compare lower-cased.
Length check uses <= so an 8-character password is rejected. Fix the comparison in check_password (changing MIN_PASSWORD to 7 is equivalent but misleading).

Registry.can lost its active check. Tempting fix: clear the user's roles in deactivate(), which passes the target but breaks test_reactivated_user_regains_access (docstring says deactivated users keep their roles). Correct fix: check user.active in can().
register stores the user before validating roles, so the error is raised but a half-registered user remains. Fix: validate roles before storing (registry.py).
authenticate calls hash_password(salt, password) while register uses hash_password(password, salt), so hashes never match. Fix the call in authenticate.
register stores the roles argument as given (a tuple) instead of a set, so grant() fails with AttributeError on .add. Fix in register: set(roles).
normalize_username no longer strips, so '  Carol ' fails the username regex during register. Failure surfaces in the registry test; fix in validation.normalize_username.
permissions_for stops before adding the grants of the root role (viewer), so nobody has 'read'. Failure in the registry test; fix the loop in roles.permissions_for.
